task.description: SECURITY-REVIEWER (WF-02 Step 2c) hard gate on REQ-158.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of INV-1..INV-8 explicitly addressed
Manifest capability list is not script-mutable

No migration, no new/changed Ecto schema, no tenant table touched by this diff (git show 48b147b --stat: only lib/letflow/engine/lua/{manifest,executor}.ex and three test files). lua_script_execution_audit (REQ-058) is unmodified and remains prefix-scoped.

invariant_assessment.INV-3: NOT-APPLICABLE to this diff's actual runtime behavior, but flagged: decision 0014 (tv-labs/lua) is adopted, so INV-3's decision-record precondition now exists. This diff does not wire manifest capabilities into Platform.install/2 (OQ-3, explicitly deferred, unchanged from REQ-157) -- Sandbox.new/1 still calls the always-empty install/1 path. No new host-function exposure is introduced. Once REQ-159/160/161 wires real enforcement, INV-3 will apply directly to that wiring and must re-verify the hash-collision defect below is fixed first, since a colliding hash would let a broader-capability manifest pass as a narrower one.
invariant_assessment.INV-4: APPLIES (live). Verified: no secret material referenced in manifest.ex, executor.ex, or the audit module; grep for hardcoded secret patterns in the changed files returned no hits.

invariant_assessment.INV-8: APPLIES (live) and PASS. The one grep hit (executor.ex:396) is a `case`/function-head pattern match inside handle_yield_result/3's own exhaustive clause set, not an unguarded `{:ok, x} = external_call()` -- confirmed by reading the surrounding code; not a violation.

result.concern_1_validate_at_load_ordering: No ordering bug inside validate_at_load/3 itself: it calls validate_shape/1 first (no hash computed, no comparison attempted on shape failure), then compute_hash/2, then a plain equality check -- purely in-memory, no I/O, confirmed by direct code read of lib/letflow/engine/lua/manifest.ex:165-180. HOWEVER: grep -rn 'validate_at_load' lib/ test/ confirms this function is called ONLY from test files (manifest_test.exs, manifest_executor_audit_test.exs) -- nothing in lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex or lib/letflow/engine/lua_script_audit.ex calls it. Executor.execute_with_manifest/2,3 unconditionally runs run_script/3 (which calls Lua.eval!/2) regardless of any manifest hash; the registered_hash parameter passed to execute_with_manifest/3 is explicitly unused (bound as `_registered_hash`). The only hash check on the real execution path is LuaScriptAudit.verify_manifest_hash/2, which runs strictly AFTER the script has already executed to completion. This is a disclosed, in-scope gap, not a hidden defect: the design doc (lib/letflow/design/req158-lua-manifest-validation.md) states plainly at OQ-4/§3.2 that 'no such caller exists yet in this codebase' and that ordering is 'a caller-discipline guarantee, not something this module enforces on a caller by construction' -- explicitly mirroring REQ-058's own accepted 'no caller yet' precedent for the audit path. Given the design was already CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR-approved with this scope, this alone is not a new BLOCKER, but it means REQ-158 currently provides zero enforced pre-execution rejection in production -- only a hash function and a gate function that nothing calls yet. This must be closed before any caller relies on 'the manifest bounds a script's authority.'
result.concern_3_legacy_bare_binary_bypass: NOT a BLOCKER today, but only because no real enforcement exists yet to bypass -- explicit reasoning: normalize_script_ref/1's bare-binary clause (executor.ex:290-292) maps a bare binary() to the implicit %Manifest{script_id: "", capabilities: []} -- always the empty grant set, never a caller-chosen non-empty one. It structurally cannot be MORE permissive than the map-shaped path for the simple reason that neither path currently grants any capability differently to the running Lua.t(): Sandbox.new/1 (per REQ-157's design, unchanged here) still calls Platform.install/1's always-empty grant path unconditionally -- Manifest.to_grant_set/1's output is never passed to Platform.install/2 anywhere in this codebase (OQ-3, still open). So today, a script executed via either the bare-binary or the map-shaped script_ref runs with IDENTICAL (zero) actual host capabilities; the manifest's capabilities field currently affects only the audit-hash value, not the sandbox's real authority. The bare-binary path is therefore 'equally, not more, permissive' as ELIXIR-DEV characterized it, but this reasoning is CONDITIONAL and TIME-LIMITED: it holds only as long as (a) OQ-3 (capability wiring into Platform.install/2) remains unbuilt, and (b) OQ-4 (a real production caller of validate_at_load/3) remains unbuilt. The moment either lands, the bare-binary clause becomes a genuine unrestricted-capability escape hatch unless it is either removed or forced to require an explicit, auditable empty manifest rather than an implicit one. Recommendation for REVIEWER/future work: track this as a hard precondition on REQ-159/160/161 -- do not wire real Platform.install/2 capability enforcement while the bare-binary script_ref clause still exists silently defaulting to an empty manifest.
result.concern_4_end_to_end_audit_tamper_detect: Confirmed by direct read of test/letflow/engine/lua/manifest_executor_audit_test.exs: the AC3 test performs a real Executor + real LuaScriptAudit.execute_script_for_audit/6 call and asserts the persisted AuditRecord.manifest_hash (read back independently via Repo.get) equals Manifest.compute_hash/2's output for the executed manifest+script pair -- proving the persisted hash is manifest-sensitive, not script-only, for a genuine end-to-end path (subject to the caveat in concern 2: this proof is only sound if compute_hash/2 itself is collision-free, which it currently is not for adversarially-crafted capability strings).
result.concern_5_manifest_not_script_mutable: Confirmed: Manifest is a plain data struct built entirely from caller-supplied arguments (compute_hash/2, validate_shape/1, validate_at_load/3 all take manifest as a parameter; nothing in manifest.ex, executor.ex's run_script/3, or run_with_heap_limit/5 ever reads a value out of the executed Lua.t() state or the script's own return value to construct or mutate a Manifest.t(). The manifest is computed/compared entirely before and independently of Lua.eval!/2's invocation and result.
result.verdict_reasoning: FAIL is driven entirely by concern 2: Manifest.compute_hash/2's capability-list canonicalization (lib/letflow/engine/lua/manifest.ex:117-122, `Enum.join(<<0x0A>>)` with no per-entry escaping or length-prefixing, and validate_shape/1 not forbidding 0x0A/0x00 in capability strings) allows two genuinely different, non-duplicate capability sets to collide onto the identical hash -- empirically confirmed. This directly breaks INV-MAN-1's own stated claim ('equal inputs ... always produce an equal output string' implicitly also requires the converse for AC5's sensitivity claim) and LUA-07's core acceptance text ('modified manifest without re-registration is rejected'). This is a correctness/security defect in the hash function itself, independent of and more severe than the disclosed OQ-3/OQ-4 scope gaps (which are acceptable, pre-existing, disclosed limitations).
fix_instructions_for_elixir_dev: In lib/letflow/engine/lua/manifest.ex's compute_hash/2, replace the raw-separator-joined capability-list encoding with a delimiter-injection-proof framing. Recommended: length-prefix every variable-length field instead of relying on a byte value assumed absent from the field's own alphabet. E.g. for each canonicalized (sorted, deduped) capability string `cap`, encode as `<<byte_size(cap)::32>> <> cap` and concatenate all of them (order fixed by the existing sort) -- this makes the byte boundary between entries unambiguous regardless of what bytes `cap` itself contains, eliminating the collision class entirely. Apply the identical length-prefixing to `script_id` and to `script_source` too, replacing the 0x00 separators, since the moduledoc's own claim that 0x00 'cannot appear inside a String.t() ... in practice' is not actually true for Elixir binaries and should not be relied on.

Alternative (equivalent but more restrictive) fix if length-prefixing is judged too large a change: add a structural rule in validate_shape/1 that rejects any capability string (or script_id) containing 0x00 or 0x0A, returning {:error, {:invalid_capabilities, capabilities}} / {:error, {:invalid_script_id, script_id}} -- but this only closes the hole if validate_shape/1 is guaranteed to run before compute_hash/2 on every call path; compute_hash/2 itself is documented as NOT running validate_shape/1 first (manifest.ex:110-113, 'Does not validate manifest's shape first'), so this alternative requires additionally making compute_hash/2 itself shape-check, or clearly documenting and enforcing that no caller may call compute_hash/2 directly without validate_shape/1 first. The length-prefix fix is preferred because it does not depend on caller discipline.

Add regression tests to test/letflow/engine/lua/manifest_test.exs proving that two syntactically-different, non-dedup capability sets whose members contain 0x0A and/or 0x00 bytes never collide, mirroring the exact case found in this review (['a\nb','c'] vs ['a','b','c'] with the same script_id and script_source must now produce different hashes).
Re-run test/letflow/engine/lua/manifest_test.exs, manifest_executor_audit_test.exs, and the full scripts/test_parallel.sh suite after the fix, and report real output.
This does not require any change to executor.ex or lua_script_audit.ex -- both call Manifest.compute_hash/2 without duplicating its byte-layout logic, so the fix is contained entirely to manifest.ex.
result.note_on_scratch_verification: A temporary ExUnit test file (test/letflow/engine/lua/manifest_collision_scratch_test.exs) was created solely to empirically confirm the collision against the real compute_hash/2 implementation, run once via `mix test`, and then deleted -- it is not part of this diff and does not appear in `git status`.
